gloss: stirring; slight movement of the body

definitions.gloss: stirring; slight movement of the body; fidgeting
definitions.explanation: A small, often unconscious movement of the body, such as shifting one's weight, squirming, or fidgeting. Most commonly used in the negative — 身じろぎもしない or 身じろぎもせず — to describe someone remaining perfectly still.

examples.japanese: ⟦{猫|ねこ}→猫：02237_neko⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{身|み}じろぎ⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧せず⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{獲物|えもの}→獲物：08638_emono⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{見|み}つめていた→見つめる：04571_mitsumeru⟧。
examples.english: The cat watched its prey without stirring at all.

examples.japanese: ⟦{緊張|きんちょう}→緊張：02494_kinchou⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧あまり、{身|み}じろぎ⟦{一|ひと}つ→一つ：02948_hitotsu⟧⟦できなかった→できる：00557_dekiru⟧。
examples.english: I was so nervous that I couldn't move a muscle.

notes:
A literary and descriptive word almost always encountered in negative constructions. The pattern {身|み}じろぎもしない (not stirring at all) is a common literary device to convey tension, concentration, or fear.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {身|み}じろぎもしない: not moving at all; perfectly still
- {身|み}じろぎ⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧せず: without stirring (connective form)
- {身|み}じろぎ⟦{一|ひと}つ→一つ：02948_hitotsu⟧⟦しない→する：00392_suru⟧: not making the slightest movement

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {微動|びどう}だに⟦しない→する：00392_suru⟧: not budging an inch — very similar in meaning and usage
- ⟦じっとする→じっとする：25342_jittosuru⟧: to stay still; to keep motionless — more everyday
- ⟦{動|うご}かない→動く：00904_ugoku⟧: not moving — plain, neutral description

ETYMOLOGY:
From ⟦{身|み}→身：01764_mi⟧ (body) and じろぐ (to stir, to shift), an older verb meaning to move slightly. The verb じろぐ itself is rarely used independently in modern Japanese.
